nodes.title: Two-pass capture: project-aware precision pass + project-blind recall pass
nodes.summary: Precision (what's reusable in THIS kind of work) and recall (catch the off-topic tangent) pull in opposite directions inside a single filter — run them as two separate passes instead of one compromise pass.
nodes.detail: Pass 1 is tuned to a one-line project-nature descriptor and applies a hard gate (reusable beyond this task AND non-obvious). Pass 2 ignores the project entirely and just flags sparks as an unclassified 'seed' — placement happens later, by recurrence or decay, not at capture time.

nodes.title: Never let a similarity threshold auto-decide keep/drop
nodes.summary: Statistics propose (score, shortlist neighbors); only the AI adjudicates the semantic call (same idea? worth keeping?). A bare embedding-distance cutoff will silently merge distinct ideas or silently drop real ones.
nodes.trigger: before wiring any embedding/similarity score into an automated keep-vs-drop or merge-vs-spawn decision

nodes.title: Two contracts, nothing else crosses layers
nodes.summary: Keeping exactly two data contracts (prompt-to-body is a JSON entry; body-to-AI/viz is graph.json + MCP tools) is what makes the system portable across any assistant that can read an instruction file and shell out — everything else stays internal to one part and is free to change.

nodes.title: Delete stale rule .done markers when extending a Snakemake pipeline's scope mid-project
nodes.summary: In individual-rule submission mode, targeting a rule-name aggregator can report 'Nothing to be done' even though new work (e.g. a newly added region/chromosome/sample) is required, if a .done marker from an earlier narrower run still exists. Verify by targeting the exact new output file directly; if that path triggers work but the aggregator doesn't, delete the stale .done marker files to force Snakemake to re-examine the full dependency list.
nodes.trigger: adding new regions/chromosomes/samples to an already-completed Snakemake pipeline and getting an unexpected 'Nothing to be done'

nodes.title: `module load X 2>/dev/null || true` can silently no-op inside a non-interactive sbatch script
nodes.summary: Suppressing module-load errors with `|| true` hides the fact that the `module` command itself may not be initialized in a non-interactive SLURM job shell, leaving the wrong (or a bare default) toolchain on PATH with no visible failure. If a script depends on a specific interpreter/toolchain, resolve and export its absolute bin path directly instead of trusting `module load` to have worked.
nodes.trigger: writing an sbatch script that calls module load before running an interpreter or tool, especially if failures are silenced

nodes.title: `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` can cause a false ModuleNotFoundError for a package that IS installed
nodes.summary: If a package was installed with `pip install --user`, setting PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 hides it from the interpreter even when PATH and the module/toolchain are otherwise correct -- the resulting ImportError looks like a missing dependency, not an environment-variable problem. Check for this env var specifically when an import fails despite pip show/pip list confirming the package is present.
nodes.trigger: debugging a ModuleNotFoundError in a non-interactive job shell for a package pip confirms is installed

nodes.title: Pick genotype-merge strategy (union vs. intersection) by what the downstream tool tolerates, not by habit
nodes.summary: When merging multiple genotyped cohorts into one panel, an intersection (common-SNP-only) merge gives near-zero missingness but can be too sparse for tools that need positional SNP density (e.g. an LD/fine-mapping reference panel needing a minimum match rate). Use a union merge instead when the consumer mode-imputes missing calls (e.g. bigsnpr's snp_fastImputeSimple). Conversely, use an intersection merge for GRM/heritability estimation, where dense non-imputed genotypes are wanted rather than tolerating imputed missingness.

nodes.title: Bumping a Snakemake rule's cluster time-limit isn't enough if the orchestrating sbatch controller has its own, smaller --time budget
nodes.summary: When a cluster job hits its SLURM time limit, increasing just the rule's resources.time (or a job's requested time) can still fail silently if the outer controller/orchestrator script that submits and waits on it has its own shorter --time in its own #SBATCH header -- the controller gets killed and the dispatched sub-job is orphaned before it can finish, even though the actual computation would have completed given more time. Always check and align BOTH budgets (the rule/job AND its orchestrator) when responding to a timeout, not just the one that actually got killed.
nodes.trigger: increasing a rule's or job's SLURM time resource after a timeout, when that job is itself launched by another sbatch/controller script

nodes.title: A mutable-looking module-level default argument (`x: Path = SOME_DEFAULT`) freezes at function-definition time, not call time
nodes.summary: Python evaluates default argument values once, when the function is defined — so `monkeypatch.setattr(module, 'SOME_DEFAULT', ...)` in a test does nothing for functions already defined with `param=SOME_DEFAULT`, even though the module attribute itself changed. The function keeps using the original value forever.
nodes.detail: Bit us for real: brainny/config.py's functions used `config_dir: Path = DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR`. A pytest fixture patched `DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR` expecting isolation, but every call silently kept writing to the real ~/.brainny/config.json — the test suite polluted real user config with junk keys before this was caught. Fix: use a `None` sentinel and resolve the module attribute *inside* the function body (late binding), not as the parameter default.
nodes.trigger: before writing a function whose default argument is meant to be overridable via monkeypatching a module-level constant, especially one used by tests

nodes.title: Renaming a directory that's the pinned working directory of an active tool session fails with "Device or resource busy" on Windows — even from outside it
nodes.summary: The lock isn't held by the shell's own cwd (cd-ing out first doesn't help) — it's held by whatever wrapping/harness process has that path pinned as its working directory for the session. A plain rename/move will fail. Copy the tree to the new name instead (and reinstall any editable pip install from the new path afterward, since it records the absolute source path).
nodes.detail: Also: git-bash/MSYS mangles Windows-style single-letter robocopy flags (`/E`, `/R:1`, `/COPYALL`) into path conversions, producing bogus errors like "Invalid Parameter #3: E:/" — run robocopy from PowerShell instead, not git-bash. And /COPYALL needs elevated 'Manage Auditing' rights; drop it and use robocopy's default copy flags unless you actually need ACL/audit metadata preserved.
nodes.trigger: before renaming or moving a project folder that a running Claude Code (or similar pinned-cwd tool) session is currently operating in

nodes.title: `git push` (no args) fails with an upstream-mismatch error if the initial push used `HEAD:main` syntax on a differently-named local branch
nodes.summary: Pushing via `git push -u origin HEAD:main` sets up tracking in a way that later bare `git push` calls reject with "the upstream branch of your current branch does not match the name of your current branch." Name the local branch to match the remote branch first (e.g. `git checkout -B main`) so a plain `git push` afterward is unambiguous.
nodes.trigger: before scripting/automating `git push` calls (no explicit refspec) against a freshly-created repo or test fixture

nodes.title: Claude Code's available-skills list refreshes mid-session when a new SKILL.md file appears under ~/.claude/skills/ — no new session needed
nodes.summary: Writing a new skill file to the global skills directory made it immediately invokable in the *same*, already-running session — confirmed directly by a system reminder listing it right after the file was created. Useful when installing/updating a skill programmatically: no need to tell the user to restart their session just to pick it up.

nodes.title: pip editable installs silently drift from the clone you think you're editing
nodes.summary: When a package is pip-installed with `pip install -e`, `pip show <pkg>`'s "Editable project location" is the actual source of truth for what code runs — not whatever clone you happen to be editing. If you have more than one clone/checkout of the same repo on disk, the CLI can keep behaving 'old' after you push/pull changes elsewhere, because the install points at a different, stale clone entirely.
nodes.trigger: Before assuming a code change 'isn't taking effect', run `pip show <pkg>` and check Editable project location matches the clone you actually edited/pulled.

nodes.title: assets baked into source code at generation time don't auto-update from their source file
nodes.summary: A generated artifact (e.g. ASCII art rendered from an image, then hand-copied into a Python constant) has no build step tying it to its source file. Editing the source file (assci.txt) later does nothing to the baked constant (_GLYPH in banner.py) until someone manually regenerates and re-pastes it. Easy to think 'I updated the source, why didn't the output change'.
nodes.trigger: When a file looks like a 'source' for something baked into code, check whether there's an actual build step wiring them together, or just a one-time manual copy — and document which, right next to the baked constant.

nodes.title: when a GUI installer needs elevation in a non-interactive shell, grab the tool's portable zip instead
nodes.summary: `winget install` for a tool that ships an MSI (e.g. GitHub CLI) can fail silently with exit 1602 ('you cancelled the installation') in a non-interactive/sandboxed session, because the UAC elevation prompt can't be answered. Downloading the project's portable/zip release directly (Invoke-WebRequest + Expand-Archive) and calling the .exe by full path sidesteps the need for elevation entirely, with no admin rights required.
nodes.trigger: winget/MSI install failing with an elevation-flavored exit code in an automated/non-interactive context.

nodes.title: Python namespace-package shadowing when cwd's parent contains a folder matching the import name
nodes.summary: Running `python -c "import X"` (or any script) from inside a directory whose *parent* also contains a folder literally named X can make Python resolve X as an implicit PEP 420 namespace package rooted at the wrong path, shadowing the real installed/editable package. `X.__path__` shows a `_NamespacePath` pointing at the unexpected directory instead of the real one, and `X.__file__` may print `None` or raise on further imports.
nodes.trigger: An import behaves unexpectedly (wrong __file__/__path__, or ImportError for a name that should exist) only when run from one specific directory — check whether a folder there shares the package's own name.
